key_insight: Power-law loss curves in LLM pre-training are not fixed; they depend on how learning-rate and batch-size schedules jointly shape intrinsic optimization time and noise injection.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a way to design or compare schedules by matching the $B/\eta$ path in intrinsic time, helping predict when a schedule will preserve, alter, or worsen scaling behavior.
method: Exact Volterra equation separates forcing (target-error propagation) from memory (stochastic-error propagation).
Derive low-spectrum scaling conditions that are necessary and sufficient for power-law behavior in each component.
Analyze joint schedules via intrinsic time $T_t$ and noise ratio $r_t=B_t/\eta_t$ to characterize scaling-regime transitions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports controlled nanoGPT experiments showing matched $B/\eta$ schedules are nearly equivalent in intrinsic time and that a forcing-memory surrogate predicts loss across schedules and datasets.
watch_item: The regime conclusions rely on a linear random-feature model and surrogate fitting, so transferring the exact phase map to full-scale LLM training may require additional validation.
paper_title: From Spectra to Joint Schedules in LLM Pre-training: 3+3(+2) Scaling-Law Regimes
